findings.description: The customer managed KMS key does not set enable_key_rotation, which defaults to false, so the key material protecting the logs bucket is never automatically rotated. Long-lived key material increases the blast radius of a key compromise and fails common cryptographic key-management requirements.

No policy argument is supplied, so AWS applies the default key policy granting the account root full control, allowing any IAM principal in the account that can obtain kms:* to use or administer the logs-encryption key. An explicit least-privilege key policy scoped to the log-writing services and named administrators is expected.

deletion_window_in_days is set to the minimum of 7 days, shortening the window in which an accidental or malicious ScheduleKeyDeletion can be detected and cancelled. If the key is destroyed, all data encrypted under it, including the logs bucket contents, becomes permanently unrecoverable, which can be used to destroy audit evidence.
